data.mechanism: One of the first functions assigned to mTORC2 was shaping the cell's skeleton. In yeast it was the original TOR2 phenotype; in mammalian cells it showed that the second complex is acutely rapamycin-insensitive.
data.mechanism_beginner: mTORC2's first known job was shaping the cell's internal skeleton. It was found in yeast first, as the original TOR2 phenotype, and then in mammalian cells - where it stood out precisely because rapamycin didn't block it.
data.boundary: Mammalian cells, yeast, Drosophila and conditional Rictor-knockout mice (JAC2004, SAR2004, LOE2002, HUA2013). The cytoskeleton phenotype was defined in cell lines and yeast; its role in intact tissue is less tested.
data.note: The two-complex model itself came from biochemistry (LOE2002, JAC2004, SAR2004).
